summary.text: 山 depicts a mountain as a cluster of peaks. Its common meaning is “mountain”; “hill” and “peak” are also recorded glosses.

formation.text: The whole graph is a pictograph: it represents mountain peaks standing together, rather than combining separate semantic or phonetic parts. Paleographic records list oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal and Shuowen forms.

history.text: The record lists 山 in several script stages but does not show a continuous sequence of graphic changes. The selected small-seal-style image is a modern redraw: its upright peaks and curved base illustrate the form, but are not an ancient specimen.
A Han-period dictionary account calls 山 pictographic and gives a cosmological explanation of the graph. This is an old interpretation, distinct from the pictographic analysis of mountain peaks.

uncertainties.text: The available account does not establish the date or lexical value of the earliest specimen, nor precise dates for the listed forms or a continuous graphic development.

senses.text: The ordinary landscape noun sense is supported; its earliest attestation and deeper chronology remain unresolved.
“Hill” is also recorded as a gloss. The evidence does not establish when this use arose relative to “mountain.”
“Peak” is also recorded as a gloss; no separate historical development from the landscape noun is established.

limitations.text: A Shijing phrase uses 山 in a landscape context, but the available record does not establish the poem’s composition date or earliest physical witness. No earlier lexical sense or semantic transition is established.

overview.text: 山 pictures a mountain as a cluster of peaks and commonly means “mountain”; “hill” and “peak” are also recorded glosses.
